clue.text: Soldiers look back -there's overhead protection

parts.note: PARAS are paratroopers, a common crossword word for soldiers

indicators.note: back tells us the word for look is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: LO is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A soldier glances behind him and spots something sheltering him from above.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade held above the head is literally protection overhead from the sun.

clue.text: Drama out of print maybe? Pretend not to be interested

parts.note: a play is a drama
a book that is out of print is an example of something hard to get hold of

explanation.surface: A stage work that can no longer be bought, and someone feigning indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes deliberately feigning a lack of interest to seem more desirable.

clue.text: Diamond old maiden dropped in shrub unfortunately

indicators.note: dropped in means these letters are placed inside the other piece
unfortunately suggests the letters of shrub have been messed up

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An old diamond was lost by a girl in a bush, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' looks like a gem but is the shape; 'unfortunately' scrambles the bush to RHBUS before 'dropped in' adds the old maiden. M for maiden comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is the geometric shape of a diamond, an equal-sided parallelogram.

clue.text: American's level plot

definitions.meaning: in American spelling, a floor of a building

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the American spelling of a building's floor and also means a narrative.

clue.text: Face looking heavenward stern or relaxed?

indicators.note: looking heavenward means the word reads upwards, i.e. backwards in a down entry

parts.note: a dial is a clock face, and slang for a person's face
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Is someone gazing up at the sky severe or calm?
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective means easy-going and unhurried in manner.

clue.text: Benders for benders?

parts.note: joints that bend the arm, and the joints exercised when drinking on a bender, as in the idiom bending the elbow

explanation.surface: Something that bends, intended for those on a drinking binge.
explanation.walkthrough: A bender is a drinking spree, and 'bending the elbow' is an idiom for drinking, so these joints are the benders that drinkers use.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm joints flex the forearm, making them literal bending parts used by anyone raising a glass.

clue.text: From car, see English country

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: Looking out of a car window at the English countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon, often just called an estate.

clue.text: Microbe — it is unusual according to statistics relating to organisms

definitions.text: according to statistics relating to organisms

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of the two words are made into an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: A microbe is described as rare by biologists' data.
explanation.definitionFit: Biometrics is the statistical analysis of biological data, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Like a salad with upsetting defect —— stick showing up in it

indicators.note: in places the stick inside the defect
upsetting, in a down clue, means turning the word over so it reads upwards

parts.note: a flaw is a defect

indicators.note: showing up means the stick word reads upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A salad dressing goes wrong, with a stick visible in the bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upsetting' and 'showing up' both mean reading upwards, giving WALF and DOR. The salad is named after New York's Waldorf hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad of apple, celery and walnuts named after a New York hotel; the clue says 'like a salad'.

clue.text: Justifier of a game with heart

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist of something is its heart or essence

explanation.surface: Someone who defends a sport with real passion.
explanation.definitionFit: One who argues in defence of a belief or position is someone who justifies it.

clue.text: Damsel good? One gets these gawps from characters turning round

indicators.note: turning round signals the run of letters is read backwards
taking letters from the characters of the words signals a run of consecutive letters inside them

explanation.surface: A good-looking young woman is used to drawing stares.

explanation.definitionFit: Both words are nouns for lecherous or gormless stares at someone.

clue.text: Biggest old foe ill-disciplined — one tending to run, when broken

definitions.text: one tending to run, when broken

indicators.note: ill-disciplined suggests the letters are out of order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A huge old enemy is unruly, liable to flee when beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightly cooked egg has a liquid yolk that runs once the shell is cracked open.

clue.text: Bird activity giving pleasure

definitions.meaning: a small falcon of that name

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small falcon and a pastime done for enjoyment.

clue.text: Someone setting out for the bookies with hope to become this?

definitions.text: Someone setting out for the bookies with hope to become this?

parts.words: Someone setting out for the bookies with hope to become this?
parts.note: a gambler heading off to bet is a bettor off, and hopes to end up richer

explanation.surface: A punter heads for the betting shop hoping to come home richer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as a gambler (bettor) who is off to the bookmaker; the same sounds mean more prosperous.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more prosperous is the outcome every gambler heading to place a bet hopes for.

clue.text: Engineers sticking to precise limit

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.definitionFit: To confine something within bounds is to set a limit on it; both are verbs.

clue.text: One needs correct method to get answer in without hesitation

parts.note: right means correct

explanation.surface: Get the method right and you will solve it immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, at once, without any delay.

clue.text: Sort of house that's attractive, not half brill!

parts.note: pretty means attractive
brill and fab are both British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses that a house is lovely, though only half as brilliant as hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', which disguises its job of halving PRETTY to PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated house is a type of dwelling built from factory-made sections, common in post-war Britain.

clue.text: Make out what's fraudulent's honest

parts.note: a con is a fraudulent trick, and the 's adds an S
true means honest or faithful

explanation.surface: Explaining what makes a swindle look genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret or understand a meaning is to make it out.

clue.text: Lean bloke appears heartless whatshisname?

parts.note: lean means thin

indicators.note: heartless says the centre letter of the word for bloke is removed

parts.note: a bloke is a guy, British slang for a man

explanation.surface: A skinny man turns up seeming cold, and nobody remembers his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are colloquial placeholders used for a person or object whose name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Area once making you sick — the reverse of well-ventilated

indicators.note: the reverse of tells us to write the word for well-ventilated backwards

explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse of' looks like it wants an opposite such as STUFFY, but it just means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an ancient region of the western Balkans, and the setting of Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Music business falling short before it is turned around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A music company goes under just before its fortunes reverse.

clue.text: Composer responsible for huge offence in middle of aria

clue.text: Bishop having religious soul as attendant

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
atman is the Hindu term for the soul or self

explanation.surface: A bishop with a devout spirit serves as an assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A batman was a British army officer's personal servant, so an attendant.

clue.text: Festival with saint recollected by early Christians?

indicators.note: with simply attaches the next piece after the festival word

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration

clue.text: They assume a stance, accepting sheriff's lead

explanation.walkthrough: 'They' alone is the definition: the band of men a sheriff raises is a plural group, a 'they'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff's band of deputised citizens is a group of people, referred to collectively as they.

clue.text: What imitates bird in tree

definitions.meaning: an aircraft flies like a bird
a broad-leaved tree common in London streets

clue.text: It's spread by the sea to catch fish

parts.note: marine means of or by the sea
a gar is a long-snouted fish

clue.text: Something very small that is hidden behind counter

clue.text: There's no time for equestrian sport when the light fades
